name: Palantir Technologies
tagline: High-margin FCF inflection vs. persistent SBC & share count expansion

filingDiffs.section: Note 12 — Stock-Based Compensation
filingDiffs.headline: SAR acceleration lifted FY24 SBC by +45% YoY to $692M
filingDiffs.summary: Market-price vesting triggers on Stock Appreciation Rights (SARs) caused SBC to re-accelerate from 21.4% to 24.1% of revenue, absorbing 60.6% of reported Free Cash Flow.
filingDiffs.priorExcerpt: We expect stock-based compensation expense as a percentage of revenue to continue moderating as legacy direct-listing grants roll off.
filingDiffs.currentExcerpt: During the fourth quarter, stock price appreciation triggered accelerated recognition of $131.5M in SAR expense; additional tranches vest at $50 and $70 thresholds.
filingDiffs.signalNote: True FCF ($449M) is 61% lower than headline Adjusted FCF ($1,141M). Watch SAR overhang in FY25.

filingDiffs.section: Item 1A — Risk Factors
filingDiffs.headline: Top-3 customer concentration edged down from 18% to 16% of revenue
filingDiffs.summary: US Commercial AIP adoption broadened the customer base, reducing reliance on top three government contracts, though federal budget appropriations remain a highlighted risk.
filingDiffs.priorExcerpt: Our top three customers together accounted for 18% of our revenue for the year ended December 31, 2023.
filingDiffs.currentExcerpt: Our top three customers together accounted for 16% of our revenue for the year ended December 31, 2024; federal procurement efficiency reviews may delay renewals.
filingDiffs.signalNote: Diversification trend is constructive; newly added language around federal procurement reviews warrants monitoring.

filingDiffs.section: Item 7 — Liquidity & Capital Resources
filingDiffs.headline: $1B buyback authorization remains 93% unspent despite $5.2B cash pile
filingDiffs.summary: Only $64M was deployed toward repurchases in FY24 while diluted share count expanded 5.1% YoY.
filingDiffs.priorExcerpt: In August 2023, our Board of Directors authorized a stock repurchase program of up to $1.0 billion.
filingDiffs.currentExcerpt: As of December 31, 2024, $935.8 million remained available under the repurchase authorization.
filingDiffs.signalNote: Buybacks are not yet offsetting employee equity issuance; net dilution remains a ~5% annual headwind.

name: NVIDIA Corporation
tagline: Extraordinary cash conversion with rising hyperscaler concentration

filingDiffs.section: Note 17 — Segment & Customer Concentration
filingDiffs.headline: Three direct customers now represent 34% of total revenue (up from 13%)
filingDiffs.summary: Customer A (12%), Customer B (11%), and Customer C (11%) each crossed the 10% disclosure threshold in FY25, highlighting acute dependence on hyperscaler CapEx cycles.
filingDiffs.priorExcerpt: One customer represented 13% of total revenue for fiscal year 2024; no other direct customer exceeded 10%.
filingDiffs.currentExcerpt: Sales to three direct customers represented 12%, 11%, and 11% of total revenue in fiscal year 2025, primarily attributable to the Compute & Networking segment.
filingDiffs.signalNote: Highest direct customer concentration in NVIDIA's public history—model sensitivity to hyperscaler CapEx digestion.

filingDiffs.section: Item 1A — Risk Factors
filingDiffs.headline: Added AI Diffusion framework & Singapore billing-location scrutiny
filingDiffs.summary: Expanded risk language detailing US AI Diffusion tiering rules and clarifying that Singapore represents 18% of billed revenue though physical shipments go elsewhere.
filingDiffs.priorExcerpt: Export controls on China have reduced our Data Center revenue in the region to mid-single-digit percentages.
filingDiffs.currentExcerpt: Interim Final Rules on AI Diffusion impose tiered compute caps across non-allied jurisdictions; Singapore accounted for 18% of FY25 revenue by billing location.
filingDiffs.signalNote: Explicitly separates billing vs. ship-to geography in response to regulatory focus on transshipment.

filingDiffs.section: Item 7 — Capital Return
filingDiffs.headline: $33.7B in FY25 buybacks fully absorbed SBC and shrank share count by 1.3%
filingDiffs.summary: SBC fell to just 3.6% of revenue (7.8% of FCF), making NVIDIA's True FCF ($56.1B) nearly identical to reported FCF.
filingDiffs.priorExcerpt: We repurchased $9.5 billion of common stock during fiscal year 2024.
filingDiffs.currentExcerpt: We repurchased $33.7 billion of common stock during fiscal year 2025, reducing weighted-average diluted shares by 320 million.
filingDiffs.signalNote: Cleanest cash-flow quality among mega-cap AI leaders; SBC drag is minimal relative to operating cash flow.

name: Microsoft Corporation
tagline: AI datacenter CapEx surge compressing near-term FCF conversion

filingDiffs.section: Note 14 — Leases & Datacenter Commitments
filingDiffs.headline: Uncommenced datacenter lease obligations jumped to $108.4B
filingDiffs.summary: Beyond $44.5B in cash CapEx, Microsoft disclosed $108.4B of additional finance leases for AI datacenters that have not yet commenced (up from $44.2B a year ago).
filingDiffs.priorExcerpt: We have additional operating and finance leases, primarily for datacenters, that have not yet commenced of $44.2 billion.
filingDiffs.currentExcerpt: We have additional operating and finance leases, primarily for datacenters, that have not yet commenced of $108.4 billion, with terms of 1 to 20 years.
filingDiffs.signalNote: Off-balance-sheet datacenter commitments more than doubled; depreciation drag will weigh on GAAP margins through FY28.

filingDiffs.section: Item 1 — Competition
filingDiffs.headline: Added OpenAI explicitly to list of competitive AI & search rivals
filingDiffs.summary: For the first time, Microsoft named its strategic partner OpenAI as a direct competitor in AI offerings and search/news advertising.
filingDiffs.priorExcerpt: Our competitors include Amazon, Apple, Google, Meta, Oracle, and Salesforce across cloud and productivity.
filingDiffs.currentExcerpt: In AI and search, we compete with Google, Meta, Anthropic, and OpenAI, including in commercial AI assistants and developer APIs.
filingDiffs.signalNote: Subtle but notable governance and strategic alignment shift in the partnership disclosure.

name: Snowflake Inc.
tagline: Classic SBC-to-FCF gap: strong headline cash flow vs. negative True FCF

filingDiffs.section: Item 7 — Non-GAAP Reconciliation
filingDiffs.headline: SBC rose to 40.6% of revenue ($1.47B), exceeding total Operating Cash Flow
filingDiffs.summary: While Snowflake reported $884M in headline FCF (24.4% margin), deducting $1.47B of SBC leaves True FCF deeply negative at -$587M (-16.2% margin).
filingDiffs.priorExcerpt: Stock-based compensation expense was $1,170.2 million, or 41.7% of revenue, for fiscal 2024.
filingDiffs.currentExcerpt: Stock-based compensation expense was $1,471.4 million, or 40.6% of revenue, for fiscal 2025; we issued $2.3B in convertible notes partly to fund share repurchases.
filingDiffs.signalNote: Debt-funded buybacks kept share count flat, but economic cash generation after SBC remains negative.

filingDiffs.section: Item 1A — Risk Factors
filingDiffs.headline: Flagged open table formats (Apache Iceberg) as potential storage revenue headwind
filingDiffs.summary: Management acknowledged that customer adoption of open Iceberg tables allows storage outside Snowflake's proprietary tier, shifting monetization toward compute.
filingDiffs.priorExcerpt: Customers store large volumes of structured and semi-structured data natively within our platform.
filingDiffs.currentExcerpt: Growing adoption of Apache Iceberg open table formats may reduce our storage revenue and lower switching costs to competing compute engines.
filingDiffs.signalNote: Key moat watchpoint—track compute consumption growth vs. storage attach rates in FY26.

name: Shopify Inc.
tagline: Post-logistics operating leverage with disciplined SBC compression

filingDiffs.section: Item 7 — Operating Expenses
filingDiffs.headline: SBC dropped 29% YoY to 4.9% of revenue — inflection in True FCF
filingDiffs.summary: Following headcount discipline and Flex Comp restructuring, SBC fell from 8.7% to 4.9% of revenue, propelling True FCF nearly 4x YoY from $290M to $1,159M.
filingDiffs.priorExcerpt: Stock-based compensation was $615 million, representing 8.7% of total revenue in fiscal 2023.
filingDiffs.currentExcerpt: Stock-based compensation declined to $438 million, or 4.9% of total revenue, as employees elected higher cash mixes under our Flex Comp framework.
filingDiffs.signalNote: Rare SaaS example of genuine SBC discipline; True FCF margin expanded +890 bps YoY to 13.1%.

filingDiffs.section: Item 7 — Merchant Solutions
filingDiffs.headline: Shopify Payments penetration reached 62% of GMV; enterprise mix rising
filingDiffs.summary: Merchant Solutions gross margin compressed slightly from enterprise onboarding but drove durable gross profit dollar expansion.
filingDiffs.priorExcerpt: Gross Payments Volume accounted for 58% of GMV in fiscal 2023.
filingDiffs.currentExcerpt: Gross Payments Volume accounted for 62% of GMV in fiscal 2024, led by Shop Pay and international enterprise merchants.
filingDiffs.signalNote: Higher payment attach strengthens retention, though payment processing carries lower incremental gross margin than subscriptions.

name: Costco Wholesale

filingDiffs.section: Item 7 — Membership Fees

filingDiffs.summary: Gold Star rose from $60 to $65 and Executive from $120 to $130, flowing directly to high-margin operating income over the next 18 months.
filingDiffs.priorExcerpt: Membership fees were $4.58 billion in fiscal 2023, with US & Canada renewal rates at 92.7%.

filingDiffs.signalNote: Pure margin tailwind—yet Reverse DCF shows the market already prices in double-digit 10Y revenue growth.
